claim.why_it_matters: Sibling '### 3.1 THE ACCEPT MESSAGE COUNT STATEMENT' (page 675) sits under '## 3. PROCEDURE DIVISION IN THE COMMUNICATION MODULE'; 3.2 at '##' (with its 3.2.1-3.2.4 subheadings at '###' instead of '####') is placed at the level of clause 3 itself, breaking the outline.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page 676 (XIV-18) opens its boxed text with '3.2 THE DISABLE STATEMENT' followed by 3.2.1 Function, 3.2.2 General Format, 3.2.3 Syntax Rules, 3.2.4 General Rules. The heading text is present in the markdown, so nothing is missing; the defect is its level. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md, line 25293 has '## 3. PROCEDURE DIVISION IN THE COMMUNICATION MODULE', line 25295 '### 3.1 THE ACCEPT MESSAGE COUNT STATEMENT', but line 25323 has '## ║3.2 THE DISABLE STATEMENT║' and its subsections at '###'. That makes 3.2 a sibling of clause 3 instead of 3.1, and the 3.2.x subsections siblings of 3.1. The outline is wrong (structural); the rule text and general format are unaffected.
verdict.corrected_description: The heading is present but at the wrong level: '3.2 THE DISABLE STATEMENT' is '##' (the level of clause 3) where its sibling 3.1 is '###', and its subsections 3.2.1-3.2.4 are '###' where they should be '####'. Kind: wrong heading level, not missing heading.
